title: Doc-to-LoRA: Learning to Instantly Internalize Contexts
topic: General Machine Learning->Transfer, Multitask and Meta-learning
claim: A hypernetwork meta-trained by distillation turns a context into weights in one pass, beating per-prompt distillation on speed and memory.
layout: 3 regions: training diagram left, distillation target middle, bar charts right
description: The left side is a block diagram of training. A document goes into a frozen snowflake-marked LLM. Its per-layer activations z0 to z(L-1) feed separate orange D2L Hypernet boxes. These output LoRA adapters ΔW1 to ΔWL, which are inserted into a second frozen LLM as an orange box labelled 'Internalized parameters ΔW'. A query enters this LLM and produces a contextualized response. A third LLM takes the document and query together and produces a ground-truth contextualized response. An orange double arrow marks the distillation loss between the two responses. A small legend sits at the bottom left. The right side, past a vertical divider, has six horizontal bar charts for 2WikiMultihopQA and SQuAD. They compare Ours (blue) against CD (green) on normalized performance, latency and memory. Ours is slightly higher on performance and far lower on latency and memory. The eye goes first to the orange hypernet boxes.
caption: An overview of D2L training (left) and downstream performance (right). D2L learns to efficiently internalize information, outperforming traditional CD while significantly reducing latency and memory consumption across question-answering benchmarks under limited query budgets.
abstract: Long input sequences are central to in-context learning, document understanding, and multi-step reasoning of Large Language Models (LLMs). However, the quadratic attention cost of Transformers makes inference memory-intensive and slow. While context distillation (CD) can transfer information into model parameters, per-prompt distillation is impractical due to training costs and latency. To address these limitations, we propose Doc-to-LoRA (D2L), a lightweight hypernetwork that meta-learns to perform approximate CD within a single forward pass. Given an unseen prompt, D2L generates a LoRA adapter for a target LLM, enabling subsequent queries to be answered without re-consuming the original context, reducing latency and KV-cache memory consumption during inference of the target LLM. On a long-context needle-in-a-haystack task, D2L successfully learns to map contexts into adapters that store the needle information, achieving near-perfect zero-shot accuracy at sequence lengths exceeding the target LLM's native context window by more than 4x. On real-world QA datasets with limited compute, D2L outperforms standard CD while significantly reducing peak memory consumption and update latency. We envision that D2L can facilitate rapid adaptation of LLMs, opening up the possibility of frequent knowledge updates and personalized chat behavior.
